title: Structural Git-Worktree Awareness in Contract Discovery

preflight.note: Stamped by `repopact new`; the work item was recorded before implementation began.

acceptance_criteria.text: The ForgeWire `.claude/worktrees/wi238-regression-test` reproduction (finding F-015, capture 016) is reproduced as a durable, checked-in fixture and passes after the fix, without depending on the literal directory name `worktrees` alone.

A genuine nested `AGENTS.md` contract (a real sub-repository or intentionally nested governed tree, not a worktree) is still discovered and validated correctly after the fix — the fix must not turn into a blanket exclusion that hides real nested contracts.

The fix does not rely solely on one literal directory-name allowlist entry (extending `IGNORED_PARTS` with more hardcoded names is an acceptable fallback layer, not the primary mechanism). The work explicitly evaluates at least one structural signal for distinguishing a linked git-worktree checkout from the primary working tree (e.g. `.git` being a file pointing at `.git/worktrees/<name>` rather than a directory, or `git worktree list --porcelain` cross-referenced against the scan root) before choosing an implementation.
Regression coverage includes Windows-style paths (backslash separators, drive letters), not only POSIX-style paths, given RepoPact's adopters include Windows-hosted repositories (ForgeWire).
`repopact validate` is proven unaffected on an ordinary repository with no worktrees present — the fix introduces no new false negative or performance regression on the common case.

The work item's own record explicitly states how nested repositories and worktrees are to be treated going forward (the decision itself, not just the code), following the precedent of a dated decisions/ record for a structural contract-discovery change.
